newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Krka says will step up investment.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Krka says will step up investment.

text.p: Slovenian drug maker Krka said on Wednesday it planned to step up investment in 1997 with the bulk of it going towards the construction of a new tablet factory.

"We plan to invest $60 million this year, up from $45 million in 1996. The biggest investment will be in the construction of a tablet factory," Krka's chief executive Milos Kovacic told a new conference.
Krka sees 1997 sales rising six percent to $332.5 million, after $313 million last year. Net profit last year is expected to have risen 10 percent from the $19.1 million posted in 1995.

Exports, which represented three quarters of total sales and rose to $223 million from $183 million, consisted mainly of sales to the Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, and countries of the former Soviet Union and ex-Yugoslav states.
"In the future we plan to increase our exports to the United States, Western Europe and the Far East, but East European countries will remain our main market," Kovacic said.
In Slovenia, Krka has a market stake of some 27 percent in pharmaceuticals, on a par with its rival Lek.
The company also operates three health resorts in Slovenia and one hotel, which account for seven percent of turnover.
Some 65 percent of turnover derives from prescription drugs followed by over-the-counter drugs with 14 percent, veterinary drugs at seven percent and cosmetic products with six percent.
Krka's shares, most of which were sold at 7,000 tolars during the company's privatisation in 1995, were listed on the over-the-counter market of the Ljubljana bourse on Monday.
On Wednesday, Krka's shares fell 23.3 percent to 16,110 tolars on volume of 27,588 shares.
The company said its shares were expected to move to the main market of the bourse in a couple of months.
